source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF abstract links https://github.com/yakamoz5/DISCO and the reading metadata supplies https://openreview.net/forum?id=TYjTWxDOOC plus the verified arXiv PDF. GitHub API inspection of yakamoz5/DISCO main at commit 9b2bcf000240b9aa545d04aac3c06de8078a0023 found only README.md with “# DISCO”; no plot/figure/table scripts, notebooks, TeX/TikZ/PGF, SVG, style, data, or rendered asset paths are present. The local corpus/visual_sources/icml-2026-5e9fe0b20cf5/ directory is absent and visual_source_files_local.csv has no target row. The automatic candidate deepmind/dsprites-dataset is a cited dataset repository rather than the authors’ visual source. Exact visual composition and numeric-generation source are therefore unavailable.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Native causal diagrams and tables use a restrained black/gray palette; Figure 3 and Figure 4 add red/blue path accents, while Appendix H uses grayscale synthetic montages and natural-color photographs. Color carries causal-path meaning in the main experimental graph and is not uniformly grayscale-safe.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figures 1–4 and D.1 are native vector-like PDF graph objects; Figure E.2 is a high-resolution raster proof graphic (the page-17 image objects are about 1029 ppi). Tables 1–7 and captions are native PDF text/rules. Figures H.3–H.8 are raster image montages (about 405×405 px at roughly 402–429 ppi). All 30 PDF pages were rendered and checked at 200 dpi.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern typography, italic caption labels, thin native graph strokes, and booktabs-like table rules are stable across the paper. Main DAGs share a node/arrow grammar; Appendix E.2 is a raster proof graphic while the other formal graph is native vector. Appendix image plates share four-panel gutters. The main weakness is that path colors and natural photographic colors are not consistently redundant for grayscale readers, and exact composition source is unavailable.

figures.label: Figure D.1

caption.text: Figure D.1. The main setting we consider in anti-causal prediction. Y is the target we want to predict using X only. W is a set of variables that only permits mediated effects from Y to X. Z contains nodes that lie on open paths between Y and X but are non-directed, i.e. any kind of nodes that lie on open back-door paths between X and Y, or any kinds of paths that are opened due to conditioned colliders. Nodes in Z are allowed to have arbitrary connections in between them, as long as Z stays a valid adjustment set for (Y,X), and the graph is still a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Nodes in W are mediators. Nodes in S are variables that are d-separation irrelevant between Y and X (and Y and Ŷ respectively). We can always ignore the variables in S for our settings as they do not harm or inform anything for our prediction setup. Thus, these variables are omitted in our analysis and discussions in the main manuscript.

figures.data_and_statistics: Full permitted anti-causal graph: grouped W mediators, Z non-directed/open-path nodes, S d-separation-irrelevant nodes, and Y/X/Ŷ. It is structural, with no numeric sample or uncertainty.

figures.reusable_pattern: Move complete assumptions into a full-width appendix graph and keep the headline graph as a simplified interface; preserve explicit set semantics in the caption.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2. Performance of all models across 6 datasets. Rows 1–3 (shaded) show naive baselines: Backbone (Bias) = lower bound, Backbone (No Bias) = upper bound (training data contains no biases, not applicable for TinyBERT and MNLI, see Appendix H.1.6). Train sets are biased (except for No Bias Backbones). Test sets are bias free. †: see Appendix B.

tables.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation across runs; run/seed count and aggregation rule are not stated. Dashes denote not applicable/unreported combinations.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six-dataset headline comparison with columns dSprites (R²), Blob (R²), YaleB (BAcc), FairFace (BAcc), Waterbirds (BAcc), and MNLI (WGA). tables.evidence_relation: Table 1 capability coverage and §4 experiment setup → Table 2 six-dataset performance → Table 4 corrected/old implementation record → Table 5 search budget and Table 7 runtime.
design_strengths: Full-width placement allows six heterogeneous metrics to share one decision surface.
Shaded rows distinguish lower/upper naive baselines from mitigation methods.
Metric labels, arrows absent but metric names, bold winners, and caption conditions make comparison compact.
design_weaknesses: Mixed R²/BAcc/WGA metrics and missing run counts complicate cross-column interpretation.
Mean ± SD is shown without the number of replicates or selection aggregation.
The table places baseline bounds and method results together, but the visual does not encode practical importance or statistical separation.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a full-width multi-dataset table with explicit metric labels, baseline shading, and condition/uncertainty footnotes; add replicate counts and aggregation rules for reuse.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7. Mean epoch run time (in seconds) across varying batch sizes. Entries marked with OOM indicate that the method failed due to an Out-Of-Memory error on a Titan RTX (24 GB GPU). While the naive tensorized implementation of DISCO hits a memory bottleneck early, sDISCO successfully scales to large batch sizes, matching the speed of the most efficient baselines.

tables.uncertainty: Mean epoch time in seconds is shown without dispersion, repeat count, or timing protocol in the table itself; OOM is a categorical failure at the stated hardware limit.
tables.data_and_statistics: Runtime by method and batch size (64, 256, 768, 1024) on the FairFace/ Titan RTX setup described immediately above. GDRO, IRM, Fishr; c-MMD, CIRCE, HSCIC; and DISCO_m, Naive DISCO, sDISCO are separated by horizontal rules. Numeric values have two decimals; OOM appears for memory failures.
tables.evidence_relation: Method scalability claim → Table 7 runtime/failure surface → Table 5 search cost and Table 2 performance → conclusion that sDISCO is efficient.
design_strengths: Two-level batch-size header makes scaling comparisons direct.
Horizontal method blocks compare classical, dependence, and DISCO families.
OOM is explicitly visible rather than silently omitted, and the caption states the hardware boundary.
design_weaknesses: Mean-only timings lack repeats or dispersion.
The inset width and dense decimals require careful reading.
OOM reveals memory failure but not peak memory or failure threshold beyond the hardware note.
tables.reusable_pattern: Show runtime and failure in the same small table when cost is part of the claim, but include repeat protocol and peak-memory context.

evidence.label: p.30 Table 7 native table and caption

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figures 1–2 move from canonical bias mechanisms to SAM; Figure 3 and Table 1 map the causal assumptions and capability coverage across datasets; Figure 4 and Table 3 turn the mechanism into a controlled counterfactual test; Table 2 provides the six-dataset headline comparison. Appendix D/E supplies full graph/proof context, H.3–H.8 supplies dataset and counterfactual imagery, and Tables 4–7 expose correction history, search budget, diagnostic decomposition, and runtime/OOM limits.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions consistently use an italic Figure/Table label followed by a short title. Main graph captions mostly define setup or color and point to appendix context; Tables 2, 4, 6, and 7 add metric, uncertainty, condition, or failure definitions. Only Table 7 states a main efficiency finding directly; several qualitative captions are title-only.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Native tables use compact serif headers, directional arrows where the metric decision is important, grouped headers for capability dimensions, batch sizes, or metric families, and horizontal rules rather than full cell grids. Table 2/4 use dataset-specific metric names; Tables 3/6 use sensitivity/performance directions; Table 7 uses a two-level batch-size header.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: The paper has no conventional component-removal ablation table. Method claims are linked instead through the SAM diagrams, controlled path diagnostics (Figure 4/Table 3 and Figure H.8/Table 6), broad benchmark Table 2, and runtime/search-cost Tables 5/7.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–3 explicitly call or are expanded by Appendix D/E/H; Table 2 points to H.1.6 and B, Figure 2 points to D.1, Figure 4 points to H.8, and the appendix repeats old results and supplies counterfactual/runtime detail.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Body, captions, graph labels, and native tables use the same TeX serif/math family with italic caption labels; figure/table text is compact but consistent. Figure E.2 embeds raster graph labels, while the other formal diagrams and captions are native PDF text.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Black/gray is the stable structural palette. Blue/red path accents are introduced for causal-role emphasis in Figures 3–4, while Appendix H.6–H.7 retain natural photograph colors. The structural palette is consistent, but path/photo color is not redundant or uniformly grayscale-safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Pair a compact causal DAG with a directional diagnostic table so assumptions, intervention semantics, and evidence are adjacent.
Use a full-width multi-dataset table with explicit metric names, baseline shading, and caption-level train/test and uncertainty definitions.
Expose unit-level counterfactuals as aligned Original/CF rows and pair them with a two-metric sensitivity/performance decomposition.
Record implementation corrections, hyperparameter products, runtime, and OOM in separate appendix objects rather than hiding failure cases.
highest_value_objects: Table 2: the full-width six-dataset headline comparison.
Figure 4 + Table 3: controlled multi-bias mechanism and counterfactual sensitivity test.
Figure H.8 + Table 6: visual and quantitative explanation of counterfactual behavior.
failure_patterns: The author repository contains no exact visual source, so graph geometry, table generation, and numeric provenance cannot be reused directly.
Small dense causal diagrams rely on nearby prose; Figure 3/4 path colors are not robust to grayscale.
Qualitative image captions identify datasets but omit selection/provenance and do not label target versus bias attributes.
Several tables report means or point estimates without seed/repeat counts or dispersion beyond Table 2/4 SD, and mixed metric scales complicate cross-column comparison.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use restrained native TeX causal diagrams and comparison tables to trace SAM assumptions into benchmark and counterfactual evidence, then use appendix image montages and cost/failure tables to make interventions, corrections, and scalability limits inspectable.
